correctness.rationale: For a weighted finite path with strictly positive edges ℓ_i and an equidistant added point at R≥D/2, every real-linear extension fixing original samples has affine coefficient weights summing one. Independent edge-slope duality yields its exact Kantorovich–Rubinstein norm N_j=Σ_{i<j}ℓ_i|F_i|+Σ_{i≥j}ℓ_i|F_i−1|. Endpoint evaluations force minimax radius D/2 and endpoint average attains it, giving operator norm 1. Equality at R=D/2 forces 0≤F_i≤1, weighted mean D/2 and every prefix inequality; these characterize all optimizers. A relative-interior linear perturbation shows critical dimension m−1, and a three-edge explicit perturbation gives first negative coefficient at four original vertices. For unit lengths, the cyclic maximum rotation lemma partitions central cube slice into m equal ballot regions; coordinate-order symmetry gives the nonnegative region 1/m! of the slice, hence fraction 1/(m−1)! of the optimizer region. The central cube section formula supplies its absolute Euclidean volume. Independently counted a fine rational grid in m=3: 2,549 signed and 1,275 nonnegative critical optimizers, approaching the exact 1/2 area proportion, without using sampling as an infinite proof. Inspected complete packaged 3,161-byte rational checker, including 11,715 profile checks and extremal Lipschitz test potentials.

originality.rationale: Godard gives the tree Lipschitz-free/L1 representation, general projection-extension works prove existence/norm estimates, and Marichal–Mossinghoff gives the central hypercube slice volume. Those prior ingredients are expressly excluded as standalone novelties. None of the inspected statements classifies all weighted-path signed norm-one coefficient sets or compares their volume to nonnegative optima by 1/(m−1)!. Parallel Resultary cycles, Cartesian cycle products and equilateral metrics have different KR constraints. Priority remains sensitive to unindexed continuous ballot/cube-center literature.
residual_risks: An indexed/unindexed continuous ballot-polytope study could already state the same optimizer fraction under a different geometry/measure interpretation.
The simple form of the 1/(m−1)! ratio should not be mistaken for proof of novelty; only the full equality geometry is claimed.
No result for arbitrary attachment metrics or target vector spaces.

value.rationale: All weighted paths admit a natural optimal scalar extension problem. The exact critical signed optimizer polytope, threshold where negative coefficients become unavoidable among some optimizers, and sharp factorial prevalence of positive weight optimizers quantify geometry that generic extension-norm existence cannot convey. The infinite m law is a motivated exact invariant rather than an arbitrary small instance.
